AI semiconductor revenues alone jumped 143% year over year to $10.8 billion, supported by increasing demand for custom accelerators and AI networking, with networking contributing nearly 40% of AI revenues. [...] Broadcom is facing stiff competition from NVIDIA NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices AMD in the semiconductor space.  
  
NVIDIA poses the biggest competitive threat to Broadcom by offering a tightly integrated AI infrastructure platform that combines GPUs, CPUs and networking. The company is rapidly expanding beyond accelerators into networking with NVLink, InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, BlueField DPUs and its upcoming Vera CPU, reducing customers' need for third-party networking silicon. With Blackwell and Rubin systems shipping as fully integrated AI factories and networking attached to more than 90% of deployments, NVIDIA is capturing a larger share of AI infrastructure spending, directly challenging Broadcom's custom AI accelerators and Ethernet switching business.

comparison_matrix.executive_summary: NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Intel all maintain a presence in Europe and the United States with AI computing and data‑center platforms aimed at cloud service providers and enterprises. Broadcom differentiates itself through a subscription‑based, fully bundled rack offering and high‑profile collaborations with OpenAI and Meta, while Intel combines a wide hardware portfolio (CPU, Gaudi, GPUs) with mixed per‑unit and subscription software pricing. NVIDIA continues to rely on per‑unit hardware sales and enterprise software licenses, but all three firms have introduced comparable AI‑focused hardware and platform updates in the past two years.

dimensions.takeaway: Both Broadcom and Intel have an established presence in Europe and the United States, comparable to NVIDIA.
